reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 19. Nay or No: 20. Not Voting: 1. Of 39 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 39 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 207 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.

This administration is full of yes-men who put their loyalty to Donald Trump above the Constitution and the American people.

Pete Hegseth waged war without congressional authorization, abused the powers of his office, demoralized our service members, and defied Congress’s repeated efforts to rein in unauthorized military action.

Our Constitution is not optional. Congress is not a rubber stamp. And no Cabinet secretary is above the law.

I’ve seen enough. America has suffered enough. I am ready to vote to impeach Pete Hegseth.

Last Tuesday, Americans resoundingly voted against a Trump administration that has bullied, dictated, and destroyed American history and treasure for Trump's own vanity. The American people demanded transparency, accountability, and a voice. This secretive, backroom permitting deal is the exact opposite. It ignores and silences the voices of so many and only empowers Trump to continue to trample on the American people who are fed up.

America’s greatness lies not just in innovation and technological advancement, but also in our deep commitment to protecting the places that make our country truly beautiful – our historical, cultural, and sacred places. In New Mexico, we celebrate our Tribal communities, our Hispano heritage, and our diversity. This legislation would hand over more authority to Trump to destroy what New Mexicans have protected and cherished for centuries. Across New Mexico, it is opposed by so many, including tribal leaders, acequias, and environmentalists.

The proposed manager’s amendment does not resolve the fatal flaws in the bill’s changes to our historic preservation process. The legislation would still give “sole discretion” to the Trump administration to determine whether a sacred or historic site deserves protection. It would even restrict federal courts from overturning destructive projects – including data centers, mining, and fossil fuel projects. As we have seen time and time again, Trump will certainly corrupt and abuse this unprecedented power.

Our nation’s growth and development in the future can move forward while honoring its past. We can reform and expedite permitting for major renewable energy projects while protecting historical places and upholding our trust and treaty obligations with Tribal governments. The reality is that our historic preservation laws don’t stop projects, they just require that consultation and communication occur before bringing in the bulldozers.  Americans don’t want to be kept in the dark about what is being built, they want to have transparency and input.

Democrats have just won control of both the House and the Senate. This rush to pass something in the lame-duck session ignores Tuesday’s great victory. We should be united around a democratic process that includes those most impacted by legislation in the process of developing that legislation. We can develop reforms that allow renewable energy projects to be built, without giving such extraordinary power to a President and an administration that has proven it cannot be trusted. 

I look forward to working with my colleagues to pass permitting reform legislation that includes the voices of the American people.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
